second_opinion.sales: Trim: Holding all numbers is justified to avoid confounding ongoing trials, but the audit and sell-through checks should proceed as analysis steps, not be held back.

reason: Sales: rejected, no change, since the shop slot is busy until 21:35 and the open_gap A/B is still running, and the warranty A/B waits for the next free slot. Merchandising: rejected as a number, since the slot is busy, and its restock idea goes to code as one merged change with sales' idea. Buying: rejected, since every buyer number is at a lesson-backed value or its bound and the FIRM_GAP 0.05 test cost 35% of points/h. Community: trimmed to pay_tips and weather at 1.0, which I read as raising them from 0.5 and 0.6 (the proposal didn't give the prior values), dropping best_value and claims because I can't read their current values, so the two moves are attributable and can be judged on a longer window.

second_opinion.sales: Keep: holding still while the floor_frac_food verdict and the open_gap A/B run is right, since 3 vs 2 deals on 43 talks each (p 0.67) is far too thin to act on; queue the warranty A/B as a single change after both close, not alongside them.
second_opinion.merch: Keep: no number change is correct while the slot is busy, and the stock-room diagnosis (127.3M of the 130M cap, 481 of 1,046 units over 24 h) is useful; its 300k+ skip rule is the same change as sales' idea, so build it once with one owner.
second_opinion.buying: Keep: no change is defensible, but check that the 35% points/h drop from FIRM_GAP 0.05 came from a run as long as the baseline before treating it as settled, and treat the 0.037 to 0.040 per-talk spread as noise rather than a ranking.
second_opinion.community: Trim: it moves four weights at once on vote gaps of about 0.6 per post (6.56 vs 5.97), so nothing can be attributed, and a one-stance-per-account rating will barely move in 2 h; change one or two weights (pay_tips up, claims down), say what best_value was before, and judge over a longer window.
second_opinion.overall: Three no-change proposals plus one trimmed forum change is a safe slate but timid for a team outside the top 10; the bold, low-conflict move is to merge sales' and merch's cost-versus-settle restock rule into one code change, with demand-ranked depth as a possible part, and ship it as soon as floor_frac_food and the open_gap A/B are judged, keeping the warranty A/B for the next free slot so the two do not confound each other.

code_ideas: One merged restock rule owned by merchandising: skip or shallow any 300k+ line whose unit cost is near or above what its SKU settles for in the ledger (our median cost is 0.728 of list against about 0.70-0.72 paid for A goods), so Book grows from margin.
Allocate restock depth by demand rank (G022ce883, Gef4d3036 and G8ec51935 lead), as part of the same restock change, so stock room goes to the SKUs that turn fastest.
forum_ideas: Find which posts draw dislikes from voter accounts near the line (our_deals drew 81) and fix the content, never ask for votes.
Name a rival in a claims post only when the ledger gap is large and every figure carries a ledger ref; keep smaller gaps in our own posts.
Keep post quality ahead of count: the rating counts as itself while posts are only a tenth of buyer ALL.

second_opinion.buying: Keep: two closed, time-normalized A/B wins support 1.1, but 0.56 is below 0.62, and our buyer's margin does not establish compatibility with our shop's pricing.
second_opinion.community: Keep: holding weights is reasonable given the short window and similar dislike rates, while rival claims should use verified evidence.
second_opinion.overall: Move boldly with bounded trials, compare equal-duration windows with enough talks, separate buyer and shop evidence, and check combined cash and margin effects; pending verdicts alone justify no rejection.

forum_ideas: Track which voter accounts hold dislike stances on our posts, to see whether a few accounts drive the rating loss rather than whole kinds.
Post claims and haggle content only with a ledger ref and a certificate-confirmed grade, since those are the only kinds that name rivals and draw extra dislikes.

second_opinion.sales: Trim: keep the shelf-life and stock checks, but a 16-minute window and pending verdict justify caution rather than freezing every change while outside the top 10.

second_opinion.community: Trim: keep the weight shift modest because one hour of per-post dislikes provides weak evidence about the distinct-account stances that determine ratings.
second_opinion.overall: Trim the package: allow bounded experiments, compare points per hour over comparable windows, keep each team's evidence separate, and coordinate stock expansion with sales so purchasing does not outrun demand.
